newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol details 1996 results by division.
newsitem.headline: Repsol details 1996 results by division.

text.p: Spanish energy group Repsol full year 1996 operating results by division, in billions of pesetas unless stated.
NOTE: No absolute figures for 1996 were provided.
Repsol announced earlier that 1996 net attributable profit rose 1.1 percent to 119.01 billion pesetas.

The firm said results had improved despite a sharp fall in international chemical margins in 1996, a fuel-price war in Britain, a price and margin freeze in Repsol Butano and a 50 percent increase in investment versus 1995.
The rise in exploration and production results was due to a favourable performance of crude prices in the period, as well as Harding Field coming on stream.
Argentine refinery Astra's contribution to results since July 1996 had also been "very positive," the firm said.

Refining and marketing was boosted by "a clear improvement in international refining margins over the year, which rose nearly 30 percent, as well as positive contribution of refining and marketing in Astra and the La Pampilla refinery in Peru."
Marketing was negatively affected by narrowed margins because of a UK price war, among other international factors.

Chemical operating results were sharply lower than in 1995, which was an exceptional year, the firm said. But despite margins on the main plastics being lower, they improved in the second half of 1996 versus the first.
Gas results were strong despite narrower LPG margins in the fourth quarter, due to no modification of the price capping system, implying higher costs for the firm.
Financial losses fell 50 percent due to less amortisation of goodwill in 1996, as well as lower financial charges.
Investments totalled 320 billion pesetas in 1996, up from 203.23 billion in 1995. Of these, 90 billion pesetas was invested in Latin American projects and 60 billion in Gas Natural projects.
Net debt at end-1996 totalled 390 billion pesetas.
